blocks.text: Place definition (scene, dungeon, realm: a place boundary is a seam; contiguous multi-storey interiors stay ONE place) Each place has its own terrain, atmosphere, objects, and spawn settings.

PlaceDef = { mode?: PlaceMode // Place rendering/simulation mode. - "3d" (default): standard 3D game mode. - "2d-side": side-scroller defaults. - "2d-top": top-down 2D defaults. - "ui": the place is its ui.js: its program (sim.js, behaviors, onInput from sendAction, world.state, place.state, ctx.place.players) runs as in any place; gravity 0. A world whose places are ALL "ui" draws nothing, boots no renderer and opens on a browser without WebGPU; a "ui" place in a world that also has a drawn place stands under that world's renderer on the 3d plane. gravity?: Vec3 // Vec3; y negative is down tickBase?: number // Hz. The room steps every place at ONE rate, the default place's tickBase; another place's tickBase is kept and read back, and steps nothing. damping?: number // The place's default body damping (`damping`: place ⊳ era default 0): the value every dynamic body here inherits on BOTH damping lanes when it doesn't author its own physics.linearDamping / physics.angularDamping. An authored value wins per-lane: an explicit 0 opts a body out. Higher = thicker medium (0 air-thin, ~2-5 underwater-thick). terrain?: TerrainDef atmosphere?: AtmosphereDef camera?: CameraDef // this place's camera: it replaces the world's camera whole, so name its behavior here too material?: MaterialSpec // this place's base material (over the world's): every object here merges its `material` over it per key lighting?: string // this place's lighting function (over the world's): the file that exports lighting(surface, lights), `"scripts/lighting.js"` sky?: string // this place's sky function (over the world's): the file that exports sky(ray, world), `"scripts/sky.js"`; absent, the world's, else the engine's physical sky inputs?: InputsDef // this place's bindings (over the world's); an action or axis declared only here reads its `label` under ctx.place.inputs ui?: GameUIDef // this place's HUD (over the world's) listenerEntity?: string // Where the ear is: bind this place's audio listener to an entity id: spatial sound then attenuates and pans around that entity's live transform (fixed spectator ears, a ring-side mic, a remote-controlled drone). Absent = default: the camera (2D, or an orthographic camera: the body it follows). The ear stands where the picture is drawn from and faces as it faces (a first-person eye, a chase camera's end of the arm), so a sound is as loud as its distance from the camera; under an orthographic camera it is as loud as its distance from that body, and pans by where it stands on the screen. Set live with ctx.place.listenerEntity = "ring"; ctx.place.listenerEntity = null returns the ear to the default. A dangling id (entity not spawned yet / despawned) falls back to the default rather than going silent. 2D places keep their fixed stereo axes; the bound entity supplies position. acoustics?: { reverb?: number } // reverb 0..1 fields?: Record<string, SerializedField> // sculpted-ground layers (heightmap-terrain skill) fieldConfig?: Record<string, FieldConfig> // per-field policy for what play may sculpt (heightmap-terrain skill) objects?: ObjectSpec[] defaultSpawnPoint?: PositionSpec // { x, z, y: { terrain: 0 } } follows the ground; a fixed y only on purpose defaultSpawnRotation?: RotationSpec // also the first camera view arrival?: string // the entity a traveler arrives by when the link names no #exit; they land one body length out along its forward, facing its way, so an arrival faces INTO the place returnDoor?: false | { lifetime?: number } // false = no way back; { lifetime } = seconds the return door stays pregenerate?: boolean // build the terrain at load mintedFrom?: string // Provenance for persistent instances created by enterPlace createIfMissing (persistence "persistent"): the base place id this def was created from. Editor/Savi surfaces use it to group generations under their template; absent on authored places and on ephemeral/session instances (those never enter the spec at all: they live in TomePlaceInstance rows). instance?: PlaceInstance // How many copies of this place a room holds: the door decides at the crossing, no verb needed. - "shared" (default): one copy per room; everyone who crosses in stands in the same place. - "party": a copy per group: everyone within 25 m of the door when the first steps through, Spawn party or not, lands in it when they follow; it dies once empty. A player `policy.admits` refuses there gets a copy of their own. - "solo": a copy per player. persistence?: PlacePersistence // How long a copy's state outlives its players: a place with `instance` solo | party, or an `ephemeral` | `session` place `createIfMissing` mints. `ephemeral`: no, gone with the last of them; `session`: the room's life; `persistent`, always: a `solo` place keeps each player's own copy: they land back in it, as they left it, whenever they return. A `party` copy is `session` at most. An authored place with no `instance` lives as long as its room (routing.persistence): `ephemeral` there does nothing, and `persistent` keeps its population's live drift across a restart. policy?: { // scripts exporting admits(ctx, entity) / onArrive / onLeave, who may enter, what happens when they do admits?: string // Script ref (spec.scripts) exporting `admits(ctx, entity)`: `ctx` stands in the place deciding (a copy the traveler will land in, else this place: `ctx.place.owner` is that copy's owner), `entity` is the traveler. A traveler from another world who lands here meets this admits() in place of the world's own, and it decides what that traveler brings in: `ctx.crossing.actor` says who comes and how (`class`, `attachment`). Where no admits() stands, a visitor's things cross only when `world.config.yaml` says `visitorsCarry: true`. onArrive?: string // Script ref (spec.scripts) exporting `onArrive(ctx, entity)`: fired when a traveler lands in this place (a crossing in, the first standing at boot). The crossing hooks fire in one fixed order; a throwing hook logs and never unwinds the arrival. onLeave?: string // Script ref (spec.scripts) exporting `onLeave(ctx, entity)`: fired when a traveler leaves this place (region-line crossing out, session detach's crossing to nowhere). Same fire machinery as onArrive. } worldBounds?: WorldBoundsDef // bottom: the y a body falls out at (onOutOfBounds) }

PlaceDef = {
  mode?: PlaceMode   // Place rendering/simulation mode. - "3d" (default): standard 3D game mode. - "2d-side": side-scroller defaults. - "2d-top": top-down 2D defaults. - "ui": the place is its ui.js: its program (sim.js, behaviors, onInput from sendAction, world.state, place.state, ctx.place.players) runs as in any place; gravity 0. A world whose places are ALL "ui" draws nothing, boots no renderer and opens on a browser without WebGPU; a "ui" place in a world that also has a drawn place stands under that world's renderer on the 3d plane.
  gravity?: Vec3   // Vec3; y negative is down
  tickBase?: number   // Hz. The room steps every place at ONE rate, the default place's tickBase; another place's tickBase is kept and read back, and steps nothing.
  damping?: number   // The place's default body damping (`damping`: place ⊳ era default 0): the value every dynamic body here inherits on BOTH damping lanes when it doesn't author its own physics.linearDamping / physics.angularDamping. An authored value wins per-lane: an explicit 0 opts a body out. Higher = thicker medium (0 air-thin, ~2-5 underwater-thick).
  terrain?: TerrainDef
  atmosphere?: AtmosphereDef
  camera?: CameraDef   // this place's camera: it replaces the world's camera whole, so name its behavior here too
  material?: MaterialSpec   // this place's base material (over the world's): every object here merges its `material` over it per key
  lighting?: string   // this place's lighting function (over the world's): the file that exports lighting(surface, lights), `"scripts/lighting.js"`
  sky?: string   // this place's sky function (over the world's): the file that exports sky(ray, world), `"scripts/sky.js"`; absent, the world's, else the engine's physical sky
  inputs?: InputsDef   // this place's bindings (over the world's); an action or axis declared only here reads its `label` under ctx.place.inputs
  ui?: GameUIDef   // this place's HUD (over the world's)
  listenerEntity?: string   // Where the ear is: bind this place's audio listener to an entity id: spatial sound then attenuates and pans around that entity's live transform (fixed spectator ears, a ring-side mic, a remote-controlled drone). Absent = default: the camera (2D, or an orthographic camera: the body it follows). The ear stands where the picture is drawn from and faces as it faces (a first-person eye, a chase camera's end of the arm), so a sound is as loud as its distance from the camera; under an orthographic camera it is as loud as its distance from that body, and pans by where it stands on the screen. Set live with ctx.place.listenerEntity = "ring"; ctx.place.listenerEntity = null returns the ear to the default. A dangling id (entity not spawned yet / despawned) falls back to the default rather than going silent. 2D places keep their fixed stereo axes; the bound entity supplies position.
  acoustics?: { reverb?: number }   // reverb 0..1
  fields?: Record<string, SerializedField>   // sculpted-ground layers (heightmap-terrain skill)
  fieldConfig?: Record<string, FieldConfig>   // per-field policy for what play may sculpt (heightmap-terrain skill)
  objects?: ObjectSpec[]
  defaultSpawnPoint?: PositionSpec   // { x, z, y: { terrain: 0 } } follows the ground; a fixed y only on purpose
  defaultSpawnRotation?: RotationSpec   // also the first camera view
  arrival?: string   // the entity a traveler arrives by when the link names no #exit; they land one body length out along its forward, facing its way, so an arrival faces INTO the place
  returnDoor?: false | { lifetime?: number }   // false = no way back; { lifetime } = seconds the return door stays
  pregenerate?: boolean   // build the terrain at load
  mintedFrom?: string   // Provenance for persistent instances created by enterPlace createIfMissing (persistence "persistent"): the base place id this def was created from. Editor/Savi surfaces use it to group generations under their template; absent on authored places and on ephemeral/session instances (those never enter the spec at all: they live in TomePlaceInstance rows).
  instance?: PlaceInstance   // How many copies of this place a room holds: the door decides at the crossing, no verb needed. - "shared" (default): one copy per room; everyone who crosses in stands in the same place. - "party": a copy per group: everyone within 25 m of the door when the first steps through, Spawn party or not, lands in it when they follow; it dies once empty. A player `policy.admits` refuses there gets a copy of their own. - "solo": a copy per player.
  persistence?: PlacePersistence   // How long a copy's state outlives its players: a place with `instance` solo | party, or an `ephemeral` | `session` place `createIfMissing` mints. `ephemeral`: no, gone with the last of them; `session`: the room's life; `persistent`, always: a `solo` place keeps each player's own copy: they land back in it, as they left it, whenever they return. A `party` copy is `session` at most. An authored place with no `instance` lives as long as its room (routing.persistence): `ephemeral` there does nothing, and `persistent` keeps its population's live drift across a restart.
  policy?: {   // scripts exporting admits(ctx, entity) / onArrive / onLeave, who may enter, what happens when they do
    admits?: string   // Script ref (spec.scripts) exporting `admits(ctx, entity)`: `ctx` stands in the place deciding (a copy the traveler will land in, else this place: `ctx.place.owner` is that copy's owner), `entity` is the traveler. A traveler from another world who lands here meets this admits() in place of the world's own, and it decides what that traveler brings in: `ctx.crossing.actor` says who comes and how (`class`, `attachment`). Where no admits() stands, a visitor's things cross only when `world.config.yaml` says `visitorsCarry: true`.
    onArrive?: string   // Script ref (spec.scripts) exporting `onArrive(ctx, entity)`: fired when a traveler lands in this place (a crossing in, the first standing at boot). The crossing hooks fire in one fixed order; a throwing hook logs and never unwinds the arrival.
    onLeave?: string   // Script ref (spec.scripts) exporting `onLeave(ctx, entity)`: fired when a traveler leaves this place (region-line crossing out, session detach's crossing to nowhere). Same fire machinery as onArrive.
  }
  worldBounds?: WorldBoundsDef   // bottom: the y a body falls out at (onOutOfBounds)
}
